facts.fact: The current Challenge syllabus is effective 1 June 2026
facts.where: information systems Challenge page, exam preparation card; the non-v2 PDF header says Effective June 2026

facts.fact: Every Challenge pathway uses the same exam content and syllabus
facts.where: Challenge page, line above the three pathway cards

facts.fact: Challenge pathways: approved CPA and CA holders; active CISA holders; a pilot for professionals with 10 or more years of experience, whose applications are closed
facts.where: Challenge page pathway cards; professional pathway page
facts.note: Pilot: only people who applied by 30 September 2026 may register; pilot test windows November 2026 and February 2027; permanency under review (https://www.theiia.org/en/certifications/cia/challenge-exam/professionals/)

facts.fact: CISA route: an active CISA, proof of good standing from the public registry and a government photo ID; no proof of experience; applications open all year
facts.where: information systems Challenge page: eligibility and steps

facts.fact: The Challenge Exam is delivered only in February, June, September and November
facts.where: information systems Challenge page: steps and FAQ; CIA page; handbook page FAQ
facts.note: Mainland China 2026 uses single test days instead: 8 March, 7 June, 6 September, 6 December (same page, FAQ)

facts.fact: A Challenge registration is valid for 180 days or until the program expires, whichever is sooner
facts.where: information systems Challenge page, FAQ on registration validity

facts.fact: The Challenge Exam has no program or exam extensions
facts.where: information systems Challenge page, Important box; pricing page; handbook page FAQ

facts.fact: Challenge Exam: up to seven retakes (eight attempts in all) within the three-year program eligibility period, in any testing window
facts.where: information systems Challenge page, FAQ on retakes

facts.fact: Challenge Exam languages: English, French, Spanish; Simplified Chinese in mainland China only (registration from October 2026, exams from December 2026)
facts.where: Challenge page, languages box; certifications page, language offerings

facts.fact: Challenge results arrive within three weeks of the exam date, from the September 2026 window (delayed scoring from 1 September 2026)
facts.where: scoring page, effective dates; information systems Challenge page

facts.fact: A scaled score of 600 or higher passes an IIA exam
facts.where: handbook, Receiving Your Score

facts.fact: Raw scores are converted to a reporting scale of 250 to 750
facts.where: handbook, Receiving Your Score

facts.fact: A pass report shows no numeric score; a fail report shows a numeric score and the syllabus domain areas that need improvement
facts.where: handbook, Receiving Your Score

facts.fact: There is no penalty for incorrect responses
facts.where: handbook, Taking the Exam

facts.fact: There are no scheduled breaks; time taken for a break counts against the exam time
facts.where: handbook, Taking the Exam

facts.fact: A failed exam can be retaken no sooner than 30 days after the last attempt
facts.where: handbook, Retaking the Exam

facts.fact: An exam may be taken at most eight times during the program eligibility window
facts.where: handbook, Retaking the Exam; handbook page FAQ words it as eight attempts per exam part

facts.fact: The CIA program must be completed within three years of approval (three-part route and Challenge route)
facts.where: handbook, Appendix D, CIA; CIA page eligibility cards; information systems Challenge page FAQ
facts.note: The IAP program window is two years

facts.fact: An exam registration is valid for 180 days or until the program expires, whichever comes first
facts.where: handbook, Exam Registration Payment and Exam Eligibility Extensions

facts.fact: Three-part route only: one 75-day exam registration extension (US$100) and one 12-month program extension (US$275) can be bought
facts.where: pricing page, extension fees; handbook, Program Eligibility Extensions and Exam Eligibility Extensions

facts.fact: An appointment can be changed up to 48 hours before it; Pearson VUE charges US$75 each time
facts.where: handbook, Changing an Exam Appointment

facts.fact: Exams are computer-based and taken at an authorized Pearson VUE test center
facts.where: handbook page, FAQ on where to take the exam; handbook, Step 2

facts.fact: There is no online testing: The IIA discontinued it on 27 May 2025
facts.where: handbook page, FAQ on where to take the exam

facts.fact: The IIA's own sample questions have four options, A to D (15 on the sample questions page, 8 in the IAP Guidebook); no opened file states the number in words
facts.where: sample questions page: 5 questions per part, each with options A to D and four rationales
facts.note: Shape counted only; no question text was copied

facts.fact: The handbook says each question that counts toward the score has been pretested. No opened IIA file says whether an exam form includes unscored pretest questions, or how many
facts.where: handbook, Receiving Your Score; exam development process PDF, Exam Questions
facts.note: Do not tell learners a number of unscored questions

facts.fact: Official results arrive within three weeks of the exam date (IAP, three-part CIA and CRMA from 1 April 2026); no immediate unofficial score is shown
facts.where: scoring page, effective dates; CIA page FAQ

facts.fact: The IIA does not prescribe the order of the three parts
facts.where: CIA page FAQ

facts.fact: The CIA exam is non-disclosed: current questions and answers are not published
facts.where: CIA syllabus page, Exam non-disclosure

facts.fact: Three-part route entry: master's degree with 1 year of internal audit experience, bachelor's degree with 2 years, or an active IAP with 5 years (1 or 2 years if the IAP holder has the degree); the handbook also lists 5 years of experience with no degree
facts.where: handbook, Appendix D table; CIA page eligibility cards
facts.note: The CIA page shows no card for the experience-only route and adds that 2 of an IAP holder's 5 years must fall in the past 3 years

facts.fact: Three-part CIA exam languages: Arabic, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, English, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, Thai, Turkish, and Vietnamese (registration from 28 August 2026)
facts.where: CIA page, languages; certifications page, language offerings
facts.note: Arabic stays on the 2019 syllabus through 27 December 2026 and moves to the 2025 syllabus on 28 December 2026. Simplified Chinese (mainland China only) is on the 2019 syllabus and moves during the December test window

facts.fact: The 2025 syllabus was live in English by 15 July 2025; the reference list is marked Effective May 2025
